scope: Rainfall intensity-duration-frequency (IDF) and design rainfall values for Guadalajara / Zona Metropolitana de Guadalajara (ZMG), Jalisco

sources.title: Intensidades máximas de lluvia para diseño hidrológico urbano en la República Mexicana
sources.publisher: Ingeniería Investigación y Tecnología (FI-UNAM), vol. XI núm. 2, pp. 179-188, ISSN 1405-7743; author D.F. Campos-Aranda (UASLP)
sources.pages: p.183 eq. (1) (Chen formula); p.184 text (a_Tr values for Aguascalientes used to verify F); p.186 Tabla 4 row 21 Guadalajara (Jal.) 14066; p.187 Simbología de la Tabla 4
sources.notes: Chen (1983) formula fitted from SCT (1990) isoyetas of 1-h/10-yr intensity plus annual max daily rainfall (PMD) of the station via the procedure of Campos (2007/2008). Not fitted to Guadalajara pluviograph data; the 10-station validation (Tabla 2) gave errors of roughly -30% to +60% (max +92%) at other sites.

curves.station_or_area: Guadalajara (Jal.), pluviómetro 14066 GUADALAJARA (DGE); PMD record 1961-1991 (27 years)
curves.equation: i_t^Tr = a · P_1^10 · log10[10^(2−F) · Tr^(F−1)] / (t + b)^c   (Campos-Aranda 2010, eq. 1, Chen 1983)

params.F_derivation: F = PMD100/PMD10 = 123.4/91.2; F is not printed in Tabla 4. This ratio reproduces the paper's published a_Tr values for Aguascalientes exactly (a_100/a_10 = 1681.185/1228.012 = 1.3690 = 94.6/69.1), so it is the ratio the procedure uses.

curves.notes: Table evaluated by this research step from the published parameters (not printed in the source). T=2 yr lies below the stated validity range (5-100 yr) and is flagged outside_source_range. Check: i(60 min, 10 yr) = 62.8 mm/h vs i_1^10 = 64.0 mm/h input. The paper is regional and isohyet-based, not a local pluviograph fit; treat as order-of-magnitude design values.

design_values.what: Rain intensity the AMG drainage and collectors were designed for (mostly combined sewers; criteria from the 1960s-1980s)
design_values.notes: With a maximum runoff coefficient of 0.5. The Atlas cites CONAGUA (2015, p.59). Printed p.109 (PDF p.55).

design_values.what: Rain intensity above which the combined drainage is often exceeded in the rainy season
Runoff coefficient assumed in the original drainage design
95th percentile of daily rainfall, AMG and nearby stations
design_values.notes: P90 is about 30 mm/day. The Atlas rain-hazard map gives the probability of exceeding 40 mm/day (2000-2018). Printed pp.99-100.

design_values.what: P95 daily rainfall at the Zapopan station, 1950-1972 / 1973-1995 / 1996-2018
design_values.notes: Shows extreme daily rainfall increasing over time. Printed p.101 (PDF p.51); Tabla 6 is an image.

design_values.what: Daily-rainfall threshold the Atlas treats as critical hazard (flooding)
design_values.notes: Fields of 20-30 mm/day already produce flooding in places. Printed p.101.

design_values.what: Annual maximum daily rainfall (PMD) at station 14066, 10-yr and 100-yr return periods (GEV fit, 1961-1991)
1-hour 10-year rainfall intensity used for Guadalajara (from SCT 1990 isohyets)
Record daily rainfall, station 14066 Guadalajara (DGE), 1981-2010 normal
design_values.notes: Same value as PMDmax in Campos-Aranda 2010 (1961-1991).

design_values.what: Record daily rainfall, station 14066 Guadalajara (DGE), 1991-2020 normal
design_values.notes: Next highest: 91.8 mm on 2016-08-14 and 88 mm on 1997-09-24.

design_values.what: Record daily rainfall, station 14065 Guadalajara (OBS), in both the 1981-2010 and 1991-2020 normals
Record 30-minute rainfall events, ZMG (1940-2005 CNA/IAM records)
design_values.notes: Equivalent to 106 and 132 mm/h average over 30 min. The same article reports 39.0 mm within 15 min and gives a 66 mm/h max intensity for the typical <30-min events. The 1997-09-24 date matches an 88 mm daily maximum at station 14066 (SMN normals).

design_values.what: Storm intensity the drainage was designed for, as stated by UdeG
design_values.notes: Agrees with the Atlas 2021 figure. The article proposes 30 and 60 mm/h as high-risk and torrential thresholds.

design_values.what: Jalisco state water law art. 86 Bis: design return period for the detention volume of developments over 10 ha
design_values.notes: Control devices are checked with Tr = 50 yr (2% exceedance). Device drainage is designed for a 2-yr storm lasting 120% of the time of concentration. For sites under 10 ha the operator's (SIAPA's) guidelines apply.

design_values.what: Peak rainfall intensity at station CUAAD-05 (López Mateos Sur, Zapopan/Tlajomulco area), storm of Saturday 27 Jun 2026
design_values.notes: Press report quoting UdeG academic Arturo Gleason, who cited ~50 mm/h as the torrential threshold. The averaging interval is not given; likely a short-interval peak rate, not a 60-min mean.

not_found: No local IDF curves or equations published by SIAPA were found. SIAPA "Criterios y lineamientos técnicos para factibilidades" (2014) is listed on sswm.info (chapter 5 covers infiltration), but no PDF with intensity tables was reachable on siapa.gob.mx.
Atlas Metropolitano de Riesgos 2021, both the technical report and the public version: no IDF tables, design storms or sub-daily station data. Rain hazard uses only daily P90/P95 percentiles.

UdG Sincronía article (González Salazar, Juárez and Loza Ramírez, ca. 2008), "Curvas de intensidad, duración y periodo de retorno como herramienta de análisis": IDF curves for ZMG stations (Guadalajara, Zapopan, La Experiencia, Tlaquepaque, Tonalá, Colomos) built from 24-h maxima. The old URL sincronia.cucsh.udg.mx/salazar.htm now redirects to a 404, and the Internet Archive was offline or rate-limited (HTTP 429) during this run. Worth retrying.
SCT (1990) isoyetas de intensidad-duración-frecuencia for Jalisco are maps only; no digital values were found beyond the i_1^10 = 64 mm/h that Campos-Aranda read from them.
CONAGUA MAPAS "Drenaje pluvial urbano": no Guadalajara-specific IDF found.

No thesis or journal paper with a pluviograph-fitted IDF equation for stations 14065/14066, Atemajac or Las Pintas was found (searched SciELO, Redalyc, TyCA, UNAM repositories). The TyCA 2024 paper with 243 convective events is about Santa Clara, Cuba.
IMTA 2016-2017 pluvial studies for the AMG (CONAGUA, 29.32 MDP): referenced in the Plan Integral del Agua sheet an-0039, but the studies themselves are not online.

Guadalajara municipal Gaceta of 19 Jul 2023 (said in search snippets to cite a 217.4 mm/h peak from the Zapopan station network) returned 404 and the server refused connections; value unverified and not included.
core.ac.uk papers on SIAPA/PROMIAP (ids 214798651, 483322181) returned 403; not read.
